tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her dissertation?

options.A: She hasn't started writing it.
options.B: She hasn't decided on a topic.
options.C: She is proofreading the first draft.
options.D: She is working on the references.

questions.cn: 关于她的论文，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她还没开始写。
optionsCn.B: 她还没定题目。
optionsCn.C: 她正在校对初稿。
optionsCn.D: 她正在处理参考文献。

questions.stem: What does the man say about his professor?

options.A: He lent many books to the man for reference.
options.B: He offered the man advice on resource hunting.
options.C: He published a lot in a number of reputable journals.
options.D: He told the man to be selective when using e-resources.

questions.cn: 关于他的教授，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他借给男士许多书作参考。
optionsCn.B: 他就如何寻找资料给了男士建议。
optionsCn.C: 他在多份知名期刊上发表了很多文章。
optionsCn.D: 他告诉男士使用电子资源要有选择性。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her professor?

options.A: He didn't think her dissertation topic viable.
options.B: He wasn't interested in her dissertation topic.
options.C: He didn't want her to rush through her dissertation.
options.D: He wasn't specific about the length of her dissertation.

questions.cn: 关于她的教授，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他认为她的论文题目不可行。
optionsCn.B: 他对她的论文题目不感兴趣。
optionsCn.C: 他不想让她匆匆写完论文。
optionsCn.D: 他没有明确说明她论文的长度。

questions.stem: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?

options.A: Change her research methodology.
options.B: Narrow down her dissertation topic.
options.C: Consult her professor more.
options.D: Follow the man's advice.

questions.cn: 为了完成论文，我们了解到女士将会怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 改变她的研究方法。
optionsCn.B: 把论文题目缩小。
optionsCn.C: 更多地向教授请教。
optionsCn.D: 听从男士的建议。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: How's your dissertation going?
lines.cn: M：你的论文写得怎么样了？

lines.t: M: I'm proofreading my first draft, and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.
lines.cn: M：我在校对初稿，明天就交给教授。

lines.t: F: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.
lines.cn: F：哦，我还没开始写呢，所以特别担心下个学期末之前能不能写完。

lines.t: M: You mean you haven't even begun yours yet?
lines.cn: M：你是说你还没动笔？

lines.t: M: The final draft is due in five months.
lines.cn: M：终稿五个月后就要交了。

lines.t: F: Of course I've started it, but I can't get to the writing yet, as I haven't found enough resources to use, so I'm still researching the topic.
lines.cn: F：当然开始了，但我还写不了，因为还没找到足够的资料，所以还在研究选题。

lines.t: M: Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research.
lines.cn: M：也许问题出在你做研究的方式上。

lines.t: M: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.
lines.cn: M：我先去问教授该到哪里找资料，然后在图书馆找到了书，还在网上找到了许多可靠的期刊文章。

lines.t: F: I've tried all that, but don't have enough to write the dissertation, as my department's minimum length is 70 pages.
lines.cn: F：那些我都试过了，但资料还是不够写论文，因为我们系最低要求 70 页。

lines.t: F: I think the problem is that my topic isn't viable, and honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material, but I was so interested in the topic that I didn't let his advice deter me.
lines.cn: F：我觉得问题是我的选题不可行。说实话，教授一开始就提醒过我可能找不到足够材料，但我对这个题目太感兴趣了，没让他的建议挡住我。

lines.t: M: Well, I suggest you find a new topic.
lines.cn: M：那，我建议你换个新题目。

lines.t: M: After all, our professors are here to guide us, so it's best to listen to them.
lines.cn: M：毕竟教授们就是来指导我们的，最好听他们的。

lines.t: F: In retrospect, I wish I had listened to him.
lines.cn: F：回头想想，我真希望当时听了他的话。

lines.t: F: But I didn't, and now I don't want to give up my topic, as I've already invested so much time and energy.
lines.cn: F：但我没有听，现在我不想放弃这个题目，因为已经投入了太多时间和精力。

lines.t: M: If you're committed to your current topic, maybe you could make some adjustments, rather than abandoning it completely.
lines.cn: M：如果你坚持现在的题目，也许可以做一些调整，而不是彻底放弃。

lines.t: M: What is your topic?
lines.cn: M：你的题目是什么？

lines.t: F: It's Depictions of Femininity in Folklore from the South of the Country.
lines.cn: F：《我国南方民间传说中女性气质的呈现》。

lines.t: M: That's pretty narrow.
lines.cn: M：那相当窄。

lines.t: M: You could find more material if you made the topic broader, maybe by including other kinds of depictions.
lines.cn: M：如果把题目放宽一些，也许再纳入其他类型的呈现，你能找到更多材料。

lines.t: F: Broadening the topic is a great idea.
lines.cn: F：放宽题目是个好主意。

lines.t: F: I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.
lines.cn: F：我先从纳入国内其他地区的民间传说开始。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the man in her introduction?

options.A: He has translated 12 books.
options.B: He is a well-known nutritionist.
options.C: His books sell well worldwide.
options.D: His latest book sold a million copies.

questions.cn: 在开场介绍中，女士关于男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他翻译了 12 本书。
optionsCn.B: 他是一位知名的营养学家。
optionsCn.C: 他的书在全球畅销。

questions.stem: What has motivated the man to write his books?

options.A: The desire of Americans to try exotic cuisines.
options.B: The demand for information about food safety.
options.C: The fact that over half of Americans are overweight.
options.D: The fact that science books are difficult to read.

questions.cn: 是什么促使男士写了这些书？

optionsCn.A: 美国人想尝试异国菜肴的愿望。
optionsCn.B: 对食品安全信息的需求。
optionsCn.C: 半数以上美国人超重这一事实。
optionsCn.D: 科学书籍难以读懂这一事实。

questions.stem: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?

options.A: The general public.
options.B: Those who are overweight.
options.C: Those who want to lose weight.
options.D: The medical community.

questions.cn: 男士说他上一本书主要是为谁写的？

optionsCn.A: 普通大众。
optionsCn.B: 超重的人。
optionsCn.C: 想减肥的人。
optionsCn.D: 医学界。

questions.stem: What does the man recommend people do?

options.A: Switch to a vegetarian diet.
options.B: Follow a personalized diet.
options.C: Adhere to doctors' advice.
options.D: Cut carbohydrate intake.

questions.cn: 男士建议人们怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 改吃素食。
optionsCn.B: 采用个性化的饮食。
optionsCn.C: 遵从医生的建议。
optionsCn.D: 减少碳水化合物的摄入。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: Today on BookTalk, we're lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans Are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight.
lines.cn: F：今天在《书谈》节目，我们有幸请到约翰·罗宾斯，来谈谈他的新书《美国人为什么肥胖，我们如何减肥》。

lines.t: F: John isn't just a respected writer, he's also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today.
lines.cn: F：约翰不仅是一位受人尊敬的作家，也是当今少数写科学题材的名人作者之一。

lines.t: M: Thanks for having me, Rebecca, but I'm hardly a celebrity.
lines.cn: M：谢谢你的邀请，丽贝卡，不过我算不上什么名人。

lines.t: F: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of 7 million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages.
lines.cn: F：你太谦虚了——你的四本书全球共卖出 700 万册，还被译成了 12 种不同的语言。

lines.t: F: What makes people so fascinated with your work?
lines.cn: F：是什么让大家对你的作品如此着迷？

lines.t: M: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight or obese, and other countries are facing similar problems.
lines.cn: M：嗯，人们读我的书，是因为超过 60% 的美国人超重或肥胖，其他国家也面临类似问题。

lines.t: M: Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.
lines.cn: M：基本上，我们都想知道怎么把问题解决。

lines.t: F: We certainly do.
lines.cn: F：确实如此。

lines.t: F: I've read your new book, and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand.
lines.cn: F：我读了你的新书，非常棒，尤其是你把艰深的科学讲得让普通人也能看懂。

lines.t: F: That's no small achievement.
lines.cn: F：这可不是小成绩。

lines.t: M: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience.
lines.cn: M：听你这么说我很高兴，因为我写的时候还担心，讲科学会让这本书更适合专业读者。

lines.t: M: My last book was written primarily for the medical community, but this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.
lines.cn: M：我上一本书主要是为医学界写的，但这一次，我想帮普通人掌控自己的体重。

lines.t: F: And how do you suggest they do that?
lines.cn: F：那你建议他们怎么做？

lines.t: F: Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight?
lines.cn: F：能给我们讲讲你给想减肥的人的建议要点吗？

lines.t: M: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs.
lines.cn: M：简单说，我主张每个人都要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃适合自己身体需要的东西。

lines.t: M: I don't advocate one single diet.
lines.cn: M：我不提倡某一种单一的饮食法。

lines.t: M: Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others, and different people need different amounts of protein and fat.
lines.cn: M：有些人应该比其他人吃更多碳水化合物，不同的人需要不同量的蛋白质和脂肪。

lines.t: F: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating 10 servings of vegetables and 3 of fruit a day.
lines.cn: F：但你对所有人都有一些建议，包括每天吃 10 份蔬菜和 3 份水果。

lines.t: F: We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.
lines.cn: F：我们接下来会聊这些建议，但现在我们先短暂休息，听一段赞助商的广告。

questions.stem: What did researchers discover about rats placed briefly in a stressful situation?

options.A: The rate of their growth increased dramatically.
options.B: The growth of their new brain cells doubled.
options.C: They began to show signs of depression.
options.D: They began to get irritated and restless.

questions.cn: 关于被短暂置于压力情境中的老鼠，研究者发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们的生长速度大幅提高。
optionsCn.B: 它们新脑细胞的生长翻了一倍。
optionsCn.C: 它们开始表现出抑郁的迹象。
optionsCn.D: 它们开始变得烦躁不安。

questions.stem: Why do people tend to have clearer memories of dangerous situations they have encountered?

options.A: To avoid them in the future.
options.B: To warn others against them.
options.C: To make good sense of them.
options.D: To reflect on their causes.

questions.cn: 人们为什么往往对经历过的危险处境有更清晰的记忆？

optionsCn.A: 为了将来避开它们。
optionsCn.B: 为了提醒他人防范。
optionsCn.C: 为了把它们理解清楚。
optionsCn.D: 为了反思其成因。

questions.stem: What do scientists believe chronic stress can do?

options.A: Produce a surprising healing effect.
options.B: Weaken one's immunity in the long run.
options.C: Make people more susceptible to illness.
options.D: Provide protection against mental illnesses.

questions.cn: 科学家认为长期压力会造成什么？

optionsCn.A: 产生出人意料的治愈效果。
optionsCn.B: 从长远看削弱人的免疫力。
optionsCn.C: 使人更容易生病。
optionsCn.D: 对精神疾病提供防护。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body.
lines.cn: 压力常被描述为负面的，但研究显示，适度的压力对你的大脑和身体都有好处。

lines.t: First, the benefits for the brain.
lines.cn: 首先是对大脑的好处。

lines.t: Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning.
lines.cn: 研究显示，短时间的压力实际上能增强认知功能。

lines.t: Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，仅仅把老鼠置于压力情境中几小时，其新脑细胞的生长就翻了一倍。

lines.t: The rats also did better on a memory test later on.
lines.cn: 这些老鼠后来在记忆测试中表现也更好。

lines.t: Scientists think the same thing happens in humans.
lines.cn: 科学家认为同样的事情也会发生在人身上。

lines.t: But how does stress improve memory?
lines.cn: 但压力是如何改善记忆的？

lines.t: It's simple.
lines.cn: 很简单。

lines.t: When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve.
lines.cn: 当你的脑细胞增多时，你的记忆就能改善。

lines.t: Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future.
lines.cn: 从生物学角度看，这说得通，因为更善于记住危险处境的动物，将来能避开它们。

lines.t: If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it's important to remember where and when that encounter happened.
lines.cn: 例如，如果一只动物遇到捕食者并逃脱，重要的是记住那次遭遇发生在何时何地。

lines.t: Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans.
lines.cn: 专家断言，同样的原理也适用于人类。

lines.t: Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body.
lines.cn: 现在，我们来说说压力如何有益于身体。

lines.t: This may come as a surprise to laymen, but experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick.
lines.cn: 这可能会让外行感到意外，但专家说，压力能让你不生病。

lines.t: Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness, but research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning.
lines.cn: 科学家承认，长期压力会让你更容易生病，但研究显示，短时间的压力实际上能提供一些防病保护，因为它增强了你的免疫功能。

lines.t: One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness.
lines.cn: 一项研究显示，经历短暂压力的老鼠出现免疫细胞反应的激增，使免疫系统能更好地抵御疾病。

lines.t: For humans, there is even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.
lines.cn: 就人类而言，甚至有证据表明，在接种疫苗前经历压力可能有助于让疫苗更有效。

tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is a common problem with managers?

options.A: Placing their own interests over their staff.
options.B: Being overwhelmed by their daily routines.
options.C: Lacking the ability to relate to their staff.
options.D: Spending too much time handling email.

questions.cn: 讲话者说管理者普遍存在的一个问题是什么？

optionsCn.A: 把自己的利益置于员工之上。
optionsCn.B: 被日常工作压得喘不过气。
optionsCn.C: 缺乏与员工沟通的能力。
optionsCn.D: 花太多时间处理邮件。

questions.stem: What may happen when managers ignore minor problems?

options.A: Their leadership may be challenged.
options.B: Their companies may go bankrupt.
options.C: Unexpected events may occur.
options.D: Major problems may result.

questions.cn: 当管理者忽视小问题时，可能会发生什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们的领导地位可能受到挑战。
optionsCn.B: 他们的公司可能破产。
optionsCn.C: 可能发生意外事件。
optionsCn.D: 可能演变成重大问题。

questions.stem: What are leaders expected to do in pursuing their strategic goals?

options.A: Keep an eye on their employees.
options.B: Motivate and inspire their team.
options.C: Sacrifice some of the immediate goals.
options.D: Have greater ambition in overall planning.

questions.cn: 在追求战略目标时，领导者被期望做什么？

optionsCn.A: 盯紧自己的员工。
optionsCn.B: 激励和鼓舞自己的团队。
optionsCn.C: 牺牲一些眼前目标。
optionsCn.D: 在总体规划中怀有更大雄心。

questions.stem: How can a manager best avoid being distracted by email? From the four choices, mark A, B, C, and D.

options.A: Cultivate self-control.
options.B: Filter their email boxes.
options.C: Respond only after work.
options.D: Check only when necessary.

questions.cn: 管理者最好如何避免被邮件分散注意力？

optionsCn.A: 培养自控力。
optionsCn.B: 筛选自己的收件箱。
optionsCn.C: 只在工余时间回复。
optionsCn.D: 只在必要时查看。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: For many managers and people who work in leadership positions, dealing with emails is a dilemma.
lines.cn: 对许多管理者以及身处领导岗位的人来说，处理邮件是个两难。

lines.t: It's likely the unpredictable, uncontrollable, and ongoing nature of day-to-day email in terms of volume, importance, and urgency contributes to their levels of anxiety and to diminished leadership skills.
lines.cn: 日常邮件在数量、重要性和紧迫性上难以预测、无法控制、又持续不断，这很可能加剧了他们的焦虑，也削弱了他们的领导能力。

lines.t: That's because it's not unusual for many leaders to prioritize email management over people management.
lines.cn: 这是因为许多领导者把邮件管理置于人员管理之上并不罕见。

lines.t: An obsession with managing their inbox prevents them from dealing with their employees.
lines.cn: 对管理收件箱的痴迷，使他们无法顾及员工。

lines.t: As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until, unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect.
lines.cn: 结果，他们忽视那些起初也许只是小问题的事情，直到不幸地、因疏于处理而不可避免地演变成大问题或危机。

lines.t: As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals, and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations, and to give regular feedback.
lines.cn: 作为领导者，人们期望他们激励和鼓舞团队去追求更长期的战略目标；同时，还有一些不那么宏大但更实际的要求：监督员工的日常产出、设定清晰的预期、给予定期反馈。

lines.t: When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter.
lines.cn: 当面临收件箱的吸引力和其他更重要活动之间的选择时，许多人牺牲了后者。

lines.t: Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress.
lines.cn: 每日邮件需求对他们的目标推进产生负面影响。

lines.t: This is because leaders must divert resources from other tasks to check, filter, and respond to emails.
lines.cn: 这是因为领导者必须从其他任务中抽调资源来查看、筛选和回复邮件。

lines.t: The solution is cultivating self-control, which is like a muscle.
lines.cn: 解决办法是培养自控力，它就像一块肌肉。

lines.t: It can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise.
lines.cn: 通过锻炼，它可以随时间得到增强或改善。

lines.t: Some suggestions include making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails, setting a timer for yourself so you don't become distracted by your inbox for too long, turning off email alerts so you're not interrupted by them.
lines.cn: 一些建议包括：在日程表里只留出你查看邮件的那几个时段；给自己定个计时器，免得被收件箱分散注意力太久；关掉邮件提醒，免得被打断。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied?

options.A: The key to increasing healthy food supply.
options.B: The best way to improve marketing research.
options.C: The impact of advertisements on consumption.
options.D: The importance of the appearance of food.

questions.cn: 讲话者说一组营销学教授研究了什么？

optionsCn.A: 增加健康食品供应的关键。
optionsCn.B: 改进营销研究的最佳方法。
optionsCn.C: 广告对消费的影响。
optionsCn.D: 食物外观的重要性。

questions.stem: How have medical professionals tried to fight obesity?

options.A: By focusing on the nutrients in different foods.
options.B: By emphasizing the diversity of food.
options.C: By stressing pleasing aesthetics of food.
options.D: By winning the support of marketing professors.

questions.cn: 医学专业人士一直如何对抗肥胖？

optionsCn.A: 通过关注不同食物中的营养素。
optionsCn.B: 通过强调食物的多样性。
optionsCn.C: 通过强调食物赏心悦目的外观。
optionsCn.D: 通过赢得营销学教授的支持。

options.A: They can attract customers with the healthy qualities of their products.
options.B: They can boost sales of healthy foods by making them visually appealing.
options.C: They can turn to marketing professors for advice.
options.D: They can rely on advertising for sales promotion.

questions.cn: 其他公司能从胡萝卜推广活动的例子中学到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们可以用产品的健康特性吸引顾客。
optionsCn.B: 他们可以通过让健康食品看起来诱人来提升销量。
optionsCn.C: 他们可以向营销学教授寻求建议。
optionsCn.D: 他们可以依靠广告来促销。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: In last week's lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems.
lines.cn: 上次课我们谈了不良饮食习惯造成的问题，重点关注医学专业人士如何努力解决这些问题。

lines.t: Today, we'll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field.
lines.cn: 今天，我们继续这个话题，但聚焦于另一个领域的研究。

lines.t: Marketing.
lines.cn: 营销学。

lines.t: Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition?
lines.cn: 那么，营销学能告诉我们哪些改善营养的方法？

lines.t: Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food, and how that influences food choices.
lines.cn: 一组营销学教授研究了食物外观的重要性，以及它如何影响食物选择。

lines.t: Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating.
lines.cn: 这些营销专家断言，食物外观的影响比我们可能以为的更大，也许还掌握着鼓励更好饮食的钥匙。

lines.t: So, how important is the appearance of food?
lines.cn: 那么，食物外观有多重要？

lines.t: Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger.
lines.cn: 研究显示，例如，仅仅在广告中看到一张诱人的汉堡照片，就能让人想象那个汉堡的味道或气味。

lines.t: This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it.
lines.cn: 这会使他们更可能去购买和食用它。

lines.t: Of course, that's the point of advertisements, so isn't that a good thing?
lines.cn: 当然，这正是广告的目的，那这不是好事吗？

lines.t: Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods, such as hamburgers and pizza, may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis.
lines.cn: 嗯，营销学教授们认为这其实是个问题，因为汉堡、披萨等不健康食物兼具赏心悦目的外观和便利的可获得性，可能正在助推一场全球健康危机。

lines.t: In fact, statistics show that 39% of all adults in the world weigh too much, and another 13% are obese.
lines.cn: 事实上，统计显示，全世界成年人中有 39% 超重，另有 13% 属于肥胖。

lines.t: Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar, and calorie content.
lines.cn: 正如我们上次讨论的，医学专业人士试图通过关注不同食物中的营养素来对抗肥胖流行，强调碳水化合物、脂肪、糖和热量含量等。

lines.t: But they've had limited success.
lines.cn: 但他们的成效有限。

lines.t: The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food.
lines.cn: 这些营销学教授认为，解决肥胖的真正办法是让食物看起来诱人，并聚焦于“看”和“吃”这种食物的愉悦感。

lines.t: That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices.
lines.cn: 这种愉悦感可以作为推广健康食物选择的工具。

lines.t: In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences, and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it.
lines.cn: 事实上，该团队的研究显示，把健康食物与愉悦的图像、体验和情感联系起来，能让人更愿意购买或食用它。

lines.t: This is a better strategy, they claim, than reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them.
lines.cn: 他们声称，这比提醒消费者某种食物对他们有好处更有效。

lines.t: But are they right?
lines.cn: 但他们对吗？

lines.t: Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots.
lines.cn: 研究者举了一个旨在扭转胡萝卜销量下滑的营销活动为例。

lines.t: The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities, but embrace their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them.
lines.cn: 该活动没有强调胡萝卜的健康特性，而是展现它们的美以及吃胡萝卜带来的愉悦。

lines.t: For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots.
lines.cn: 例如，广告聚焦于胡萝卜鲜亮美丽的橙色和爽脆的口感。

lines.t: The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%.
lines.cn: 该活动使产品销量提升了 10% 以上，效果惊人。

lines.t: The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.
lines.cn: 研究者相信，其他公司也可以用类似的广告——把产品描绘得吸引人、带来愉悦——来提升健康食品的销量。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?

options.A: It has witnessed a spectacular surge in demand.
options.B: It has met much criticism from environmentalists.
options.C: It has seen more small businesses offering environment-friendly products.

questions.stem: What are some customers doing to help promote non-traditional cleaning products?

options.A: Purchasing only this kind of products for home cleaning.

options.C: Demonstrating on TV how effective these products are.
options.D: Telling one another about their incomparable virtues.

optionsCn.A: 只购买这类产品用于家庭清洁。
optionsCn.B: 在社交媒体上给它们写好评。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s.
lines.cn: 家用清洁产品行业真正起步是在 20 世纪 50 年代。

lines.t: Prior to that, resourceful housewives who had grown up in a less prosperous era relied on substances that they used in their kitchens, such as vinegar used to clean windows.
lines.cn: 在那之前，在不那么富裕的年代长大的、善于持家的家庭主妇，靠的是厨房里就有的东西，比如用醋擦窗户。

lines.t: Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year and is dominated by large global companies.
lines.cn: 如今，家用清洁产品行业每年产值数十亿美元，由大型跨国公司主导。

lines.t: In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products.
lines.cn: 然而近年来，许多国家出现了大量提供更环保清洁产品的小型商家和公司。

lines.t: And they're doing good business, too.
lines.cn: 而且它们生意也不错。

lines.t: One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues.
lines.cn: 原因之一是消费者对环境和可持续性问题的意识在增强。

lines.t: They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals.
lines.cn: 他们还想让家成为一个没有有毒化学物质的安全之地。

lines.t: The third reason is people's awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater.
lines.cn: 第三个原因是，人们对技术的意识和了解前所未有地高。

lines.t: In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results.
lines.cn: 过去，人们可能对声称能达到惊人清洁效果的新产品心存怀疑。

lines.t: But they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.
lines.cn: 但现在他们相信技术有能力做到曾被认为不可能的事。

lines.t: There is perhaps no better example of this than a patented cloth sold by one company which remarkably uses only water rather than traditional cleaning products.
lines.cn: 也许最好的例子是某公司出售的一种专利抹布，它出色地只用清水而不用传统清洁产品。

lines.t: The company claims its cloth lifts, traps, and removes dirt and bacteria.
lines.cn: 该公司声称它的抹布能吸附、锁住并清除污垢和细菌。

lines.t: And considering that people don't see these products in shops or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.
lines.cn: 考虑到人们既不在商店里看到这些产品，也没在电视或报刊上看到它们的广告，这一增长可谓相当迅猛。

lines.t: Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets.
lines.cn: 这些公司背后的许多人，最初是靠在当地集市上售卖来检验产品可行性的。

lines.t: Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media praising their virtues.
lines.cn: 随后，在许多情况下，顾客在社交媒体上留下大量好评，等于替这些产品做了营销。

lines.t: There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness and the benefits of having a clean home.
lines.cn: 还有电视节目和书籍专门讲如何保持家居整洁干净，以及拥有一个干净家的好处。

lines.t: Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people feel they can control in an increasingly out-of-control world.
lines.cn: 在这个越来越失控的世界里，拥有一个安全干净的家，也许是人们觉得还能掌控的一件事。

lines.t: And there are social media celebrities.
lines.cn: 另外还有社交媒体网红。

lines.t: One woman in Britain has become a social media sensation with more than two million followers for her cleaning tips page.
lines.cn: 英国一位女士的清洁技巧页面拥有两百多万粉丝，成了社交媒体上的红人。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual.
lines.cn: 往喷泉里扔零钱是一项历史悠久的仪式。

lines.t: Throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true.
lines.cn: 把一枚硬币扔进水里，你的愿望也许就会实现。

lines.t: But all that money has to go somewhere.
lines.cn: 但所有这些钱总得有个去处。

lines.t: Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters, and euros could clog up the fountain's works.
lines.cn: 否则，越积越多的便士、两角五分币和欧元硬币可能会堵塞喷泉的机械装置。

lines.t: Today, I'm going to talk about where all the coins go.
lines.cn: 今天我要讲的，就是这些硬币都去了哪里。

lines.t: Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places, from fountain maintenance to charity or public service.
lines.cn: 收集起来的硬币可以去各种不同的地方，从喷泉维护到慈善或公共服务。

lines.t: In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountain's maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don't mind getting their hands wet often get to it first.
lines.cn: 比如在纽约市，从公园喷泉里收集的硬币通常用于喷泉自身的维护，不过不介意弄湿手的企业主往往先一步把它们捞走。

lines.t: There are over 50 beautiful, decorative display fountains in New York City parks.
lines.cn: 纽约市的公园里有 50 多座漂亮、具装饰性的景观喷泉。

lines.t: They are cleaned by the park's staff every few weeks.
lines.cn: 公园员工每隔几周清洗一次。

lines.t: But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers, and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
lines.cn: 但大部分硬币早已被有生意头脑的纽约人捞走，剩下的可收集量并不大。

lines.t: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul.
lines.cn: 不过其他城市的收获要可观得多。

lines.t: Take, for example, Rome's famous Trevi Fountain.
lines.cn: 以罗马著名的特雷维喷泉为例。

lines.t: For hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return.
lines.cn: 数百年来，游客们一直把硬币从肩头抛进喷泉，以求自己还会重返罗马。

lines.t: So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day.
lines.cn: 投币的游客如此之多，罗马官员每晚都要清洗喷泉，据说每天能从世界各地游客那里收到多达 4000 美元的零钱。

lines.t: Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy, and collecting that cash is serious business.
lines.cn: 每晚收集的大部分钱用于为贫困者经营一家超市，而收集这些现金是件严肃的事。

lines.t: Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain.
lines.cn: 罗马官员对任何被逮到从喷泉里捞硬币的人历来都很严厉。

lines.t: In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them.
lines.cn: 2005 年的一起案件中，四名喷泉清洁工在收集硬币后被发现把钱塞进自己口袋，随后被警方逮捕。

lines.t: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
lines.cn: 当局最终抓获了臭名昭著的小偷托马斯·摩根，他 34 年间用一根磁力棒从喷泉里捞走数千美元零钱，随后被禁止靠近该喷泉。

lines.t: For the most part, money collected from privately owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity.
lines.cn: 在美国，私人所有的喷泉所收集的钱大多也用于慈善。

lines.t: The fountain in New York City's Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not-for-profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance.
lines.cn: 纽约市布赖恩特公园的喷泉由一家非营利公司拥有和运营，清洁工收集的现金被用于喷泉自身的维护。

lines.t: Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains, and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state.
lines.cn: 佛罗里达州华特迪士尼世界的许愿井、喷泉和池塘里取出的数万美元硬币，每年都捐出来支持该州的寄养儿童。

lines.t: Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.
lines.cn: 无论往喷泉里投币后你的愿望是否实现，你都可以放心，这些零钱很可能会去到需要它的人手里。
